statement.excerpt: As more internet content is created, either partially or entirely through generative AI, the models themselves will find themselves increasingly inbred, training themselves on content written by their own models which are, on some level, permanently locked in 2023, before the advent of a tool that is specifically intended to replace content created by human beings.
statement.document_title: Are We Watching The Internet Die?

from_speaker: As more internet content is created
partially or entirely through generative AI
models themselves will find themselves increasingly inbred
training themselves on content written by their own models
on some level, permanently locked in 2023
our_interpretation: The antecedent is growth in AI-generated internet content.
The predicted outcome is increasing recursive dependence on earlier model outputs in subsequent model training, with resulting homogenization or loss of fresh human information.
The qualified reference to being locked in 2023 is read as a claim about information ancestry, not an exact technical cutoff shared by every model.
The claim concerns the trajectory of models trained from the internet. Deliberately constructed laboratory feedback loops alone do not establish that trajectory.
criteria.support_condition: Longitudinal training-data and model analyses show that growing AI web content increasingly enters successive models' training sets, creates recursive ancestry and produces the predicted narrowing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable analyses show that successive models avoid increasing recursive dependence or retain diverse fresh information despite the antecedent. A limited successful mitigation is counterevidence but does not settle an unlimited forecast.

evidence.locator: Abstract; supporting measurements in the corpus analysis
evidence.publisher: arXiv; University of Maryland and Pangram Labs researchers
evidence.explanation: The study reports an increasing detector-labeled AI share in FineWeb-filtered Common Crawl text, reaching 31.1% in August 2026. Its 800-model experiments show possible benefits and harms, but do not track recursive ancestry across successive deployed model generations.

The paper finds different outcomes when synthetic data replace earlier data versus accumulate alongside retained data. This challenges inevitability, but experimental mitigation does not establish what happened in undisclosed production training corpora.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A longitudinal audit linking growing AI web content to actual training mixtures, recursive provenance and declining diversity or fresh information across successive model generations.
